extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in media criticism, journalism ethics, and political commentary
extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper/online opinion column critiquing a magazine's journalistic practices and ideological positioning, using examples of fabrication, plagiarism, and editorial failures. The piece argues standards by contrast (what the magazine did wrong).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual accuracy / no fabrication
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters must not invent facts, sources, or events; journalism should be factually reliable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article documents Stephen Glass's method: layering partly true and fabricated facts up to 'a complete whopper' and inventing organizations, business cards, newsletters, answering-machine messages and websites to support lies. Anti-pattern: publishing stories built on fabricated details and phony sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source verification and corroboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors and journalists must verify sources and corroborate claims rather than accept them at face value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Glass's ability to persuade editors depended on unverified 'series of lies behind that lie.' Guidance implied: verify organizations, check business cards/websites, independently confirm quotes and claims before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid plagiarism / ensure originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers must not plagiarize others' work; publications must check for and respond to documented plagiarism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Ruth Shalit and the Washington Post documenting plagiarized passages and dozens of errors; anti-pattern: letting plagiarized content appear without correction or accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate labeling of genre and ideology
rubrics_metrics.description: A publication should honestly represent whether its content is non-fiction or opinion, and should not mislabel its ideological stance (e.g., calling itself 'liberal' if it predominantly advances another position).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author accuses the New Republic of living 'not one lie, but two: the pretense that it was (1) non-fiction and (2) liberal.' Guidance: avoid misbranding and be transparent about editorial stance and genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding and correcting slanderous or dishonest claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications must not spread slander or factually challenged accusations; if falsehoods are exposed they should be retracted or corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Beinart spreading a slander about the National Education Association even after exposure of the dishonesty. Anti-pattern: continuing to spread discredited claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative selection of commentators (honest representation of viewpoints)
rubrics_metrics.description: When presenting pundits as representing a particular political perspective, choose commentators who genuinely reflect that perspective rather than center/right voices masquerading as 'liberal.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NR is criticized for sending center and right figures to represent 'liberal' viewpoints on TV, thereby usurping airtime from genuine liberals; guidance: ensure panels and media appearances reflect claimed ideological labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial responsibility and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should exercise editorial judgment, correct errors, and avoid duplicitous behavior that misleads audiences about the publication's values or the reliability of its content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beinart is called duplicitous for smearing critics and continuing false claims; guidance: editors must hold writers accountable and not perpetuate disinformation for ideological aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and authenticity of staff voices
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications should have genuine diversity among staff and contributors and avoid tokenistic promotion of commentators who primarily serve the publication's ideological patrons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes that the NR 'seems never to have had a single black staff writer' and favors 'bootstrap blacks' who align with conservative patrons; guidance: recruit and elevate a range of authentic voices rather than ideologically convenient tokens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid ideological bias that privileges one foreign-policy agenda
rubrics_metrics.description: A magazine should avoid consistently promoting a single ideological foreign-policy line (e.g., uncritical support for interventions) without balanced critique and evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece documents a steady supportive drumbeat for Reagan-era foreign policy and cheerleading for groups involved in atrocities; guidance: balance and critical scrutiny are required, especially on matters that lead to serious consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportional responsibility given influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications with disproportionate influence relative to circulation bear heightened responsibility to be accurate and honest because they shape public discourse outsize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NR's small circulation but large impact as a source of TV talking heads is cited; guidance: influential outlets must exercise stricter fact-checking and ethical standards.
